definitions.explanation: A pointed metal pin with a flat head, hammered into wood or other materials to hold things together.

examples.english: Hammer a nail into the wall.

examples.japanese: {釘|くぎ}を{抜|ぬ}くのを{手伝|てつだ}ってくれない？
examples.english: Could you help me pull out this nail?

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{息子|むすこ}に、{遅|おそ}く{帰|かえ}らないようにと{釘|くぎ}を{刺|さ}した。
examples.english: She warned her son not to come home late.
examples.notes: [Note: {釘|くぎ}を{刺|さ}す is an idiom meaning 'to warn, to caution']

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{板|いた}から{釘|くぎ}が{飛|と}び{出|だ}していて{危|あぶ}ない。
examples.english: There are nails sticking out of the old board, which is dangerous.

examples.japanese: {棚|たな}を{作|つく}るために{金槌|かなづち}で{釘|くぎ}を{何本|なんぼん}も{打|う}ったので、{手|て}が{痛|いた}くなった。
examples.english: My hand started hurting because I hammered in so many nails to build the shelf.

notes:
{釘|くぎ} is a metal nail used in construction and woodworking. Counted with {本|ほん}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {釘|くぎ}を{打|う}つ: to hammer a nail
- {釘|くぎ}を{抜|ぬ}く: to pull out a nail

IDIOMS:
- {釘|くぎ}を{刺|さ}す: to give a firm warning, to caution someone (literally "to stab with a nail")
- {釘付|くぎづ}けになる: to be riveted, unable to look away (literally "nailed down")

USAGE:
In everyday life, {釘|くぎ}を{刺|さ}す is the most commonly encountered expression. It means to clearly warn someone in advance so they don't forget or act carelessly.

RELATED:
- ネジ / {螺子|ねじ}: screw
- {金槌|かなづち}: hammer
